headline: NVIDIA and an Indian university lab announced a huge set of machine-translated training text for 22 Indian languages.
score_reason: Significant open resource for under-served languages, but not yet released and results are the company's own.
importance_line: Speakers of India's 22 official languages stand to gain better AI tools, but the data is translated from English, mostly checked by machines, and not yet available.
source: Unite.AI, reporting an NVIDIA and AI4Bharat announcement
summary: Unite.AI reports that NVIDIA and AI4Bharat, a research lab at IIT Madras, announced a corpus of about 2.8 trillion tokens (word-sized pieces of text used to train AI) translated from English into 22 Indian languages, plus the open tools used to make it; the corpus is due for release soon. NVIDIA says continued training with Indic data lifted five benchmark scores by about 5 to 10 percentage points, but it warns that translated text cannot replace text written natively, that checking was mostly automated, and that errors remain.
notes: Benchmark gains are NVIDIA's claims; the report notes the effect of the synthetic corpus alone was not isolated.
